class.name: NetwPredictConsumePlan
class.brief_description: Whether one transition has an authored command to consume, and what to do when it does not.
class.description: Answers one question ahead of driving a transition: is there input to consume, and if the caller's own tick has none, is a later one already known to exist. [method eligible] gates every other member; while it is [code]false[/code] no input has arrived yet for this transition at all, and a caller waits rather than treating the gap as a decision. [br][br]When [method missing] is [code]true[/code], this transition itself carries no fresh command but a later one is already known, so the gap must be filled one way or another. [method use_last] says whether the fill repeats the most recent known command, the policy that lets a transition run rather than stall on a single dropped input. [method run] is [code]true[/code] whenever a transition should actually be driven this pass: always for fresh input, and for a missing one only when [method use_last] holds or the schedule itself runs every frame regardless of freshness.

method.name: eligible
method.description: Whether this transition has anything to decide about at all: either a fresh command arrived, or a later one is already known so the gap is a real decision rather than an unopened future.

method.name: kind
method.description: The drive kind this consumption plans for: [code]1[/code] fresh when [method eligible] and not [method missing], or [code]6[/code] missing otherwise. [code]0[/code] while [method eligible] is [code]false[/code].

method.name: missing
method.description: Whether this transition's own command never arrived, even though a later one already has. Implies [method eligible].

method.name: run
method.description: Whether this transition should be driven this pass. Always [code]true[/code] for fresh input, and for [method missing] input only when [method use_last] holds or the schedule runs every frame regardless of freshness.

method.name: use_last
method.description: Whether a [method missing] transition should be filled by repeating the most recently known command, rather than left undriven until a fresh one arrives. Only meaningful when [method missing] is [code]true[/code].
